teach.heading: Price moves because buyers and sellers are fighting for control.
teach.body: Buyers think price should go higher. Sellers think price should go lower. When buyers are stronger, price lifts. When sellers are stronger, price drops. That's what candles are showing you in real time — who won that moment.
teach.dayliNote: The body matters more than the drama. Long wicks can look dramatic, but the body tells you where price actually settled — later in ICC, close beats wick.

experience.intro: Walk the same idea forward — control can change mid-story.

steps.prompt: A string of strong green closes with only shallow pullbacks is playing out. Who's in control?

options.label: Buyers
options.feedback: Right — repeated strong closes with shallow pullbacks is buyers winning again and again.

options.label: Sellers
options.feedback: Sellers haven't managed a real pullback here — buyers are still winning this stretch.

steps.prompt: One candle wicks down sharply intraday but closes back near its high. Did sellers actually take control of that candle?

options.label: No — the wick shows sellers tried, but the close shows buyers still won that candle
options.feedback: Right — the close is the scoreboard. A deep wick that gets reclaimed is buyers defending, not losing.

options.label: Yes — any deep wick down means sellers won
options.feedback: A wick alone doesn't decide the winner — where the candle actually closed does.

steps.prompt: Then a candle closes below the most recent higher low, with only a small wick below it — mostly real body below the level. What does that tell you?

options.label: Sellers just won a real battle — a close-based loss of the level, not just a wick
options.feedback: Exactly. A clean close below a level that had been holding is a genuine change of control.

options.label: It's meaningless without more candles
options.feedback: One candle can absolutely be meaningful if it closes cleanly through a level that mattered.

reinforce.question: A string of strong green closes with small pullbacks usually means:
A candle wicks below a key higher low intraday but closes back above it by the end of the period. Did sellers take control of that candle? Explain why or why not.
reinforce.modelAnswer: No — the wick shows sellers pushed and tested the level, but the close shows buyers reclaimed it before the period ended. The close is what decides who actually won that candle; the wick just shows how far the fight went.
